proposals.impact: convert 4 stalled intro-screen sessions into quiz starts
proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours the quiz logged 4 sessions, 0 starts, and 0 completions. Every session stopped at intro_load, which means visitors loaded the intro screen and left without pressing anything. No source completed. This is a cold-entry problem: the intro screen is not giving someone a strong enough reason to tap the first button.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the intro screen headline and sub-copy to make the first line specific enough that Joel's ICP (25-35, earns well, doesn't build) reads it and thinks "that's me." The current text (reproduced below) opens with a generic competence claim. Replace it with a line rooted in the lived situation: good income, nothing to show, quiet discomfort about it. Keep the CTA button label, change nothing else. One file, one text block.
proposals.current_text:
Discover your money personality

Answer 8 quick questions and find out what's really driving your financial decisions — so you can finally start making progress.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does your bank account tell a different story?

Joel built a six-figure income and still found a gym bag stuffed with unopened post sitting next to his desk. Eight questions. A clear read on the pattern underneath your numbers.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate closer to Money Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: Money Vigilance emails are opening at 66.67% (12 sent, 8 opens). Money Worship is at 37.5% (16 sent, 6 opens). That is a 29-point gap. Both automations are live and targeting comparable small audiences, so the gap is most likely a subject-line problem rather than a list-quality problem. The Money Vigilance subject line is doing something the Money Worship subject line is not: it probably names a specific feeling the reader already has rather than a category label they haven't adopted yet.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship automation. The goal is to name a feeling the reader already has before they picked up the quiz, not to describe them using a personality-type label. Do not change the body copy. One file, one line.
proposals.current_text: subject: You're a Money Worshipper — here's what that means
proposals.new_text: subject: The reason you keep thinking more money will finally fix it

proposals.impact: restore failed workflow so competitive intelligence resumes
proposals.observation: The Funnel-Hack Digest workflow failed at 11:56 on 29 May. It is the only failed run out of 13. The failure is recent and isolated, which means it is most likely a transient API timeout or a token expiry rather than a structural code problem. The workflow is blocked from direct edit under safety rules, but the most common first fix for a single isolated failure is to re-trigger the run manually, confirm it passes, and then read the error log only if it fails again. Fred cannot re-trigger CI directly, but can write a clear remediation note into the ops log so Joel does it in under two minutes.
proposals.proposal: Append a one-line remediation note to the ops log so Joel sees the failed workflow when he opens his morning review and can re-run it with one click before the next digest window closes. The note names the workflow, the failure time, and the exact manual action required. No code change needed.
